summary: FAIL on one major finding (RV414-1-1), inherited from v4.1.2 but directly against the amendment's purpose: on the package's own bootstrap, the .NET runners, including both corrected ones, exit 0 while running no test, because the CPM test projects get no FSharp.Core and xunit skips every assembly. No package check detects it. The amendment itself is otherwise sound and narrowly scoped. v41 --check passes X01-X21 for v4.1.4 (exit 0). v4.1.2 and v4.1.1 regenerate byte for byte, and v4.1.2 equals its tag. In the verification plan only the six runner values differ: the JSON is equal with runner removed, and the same 11 suites and 804 tests appear in the same order. Contracts, state machines, layout tests and the other carried files are identical. execution-dag, schedule and validation-report differ only in version strings and the X21 row. Each corrected runner has one dotnet target (Causa.slnx), or selects --config playwright.config.ts naming only chromium or webkit, which the bootstrapped config defines. A simulation confirms that each of the 792 dotnet and playwright plan tests is selected by exactly its own suite's runner. suiteRunners cite ODR-V414-01/-02 and APR-V414-OWNER-1, an owner-authored commit (8b1d628) recording option A for both. Option A is what the package applies, and the runners and the requests are unchanged since that commit. The bootstrap writes playwright.config.ts with chromium and webkit, Causa.slnx builds, and with probe specs all four Playwright runners list exactly their folder and engine. The offline suite passes. Four minor findings: stale ODR status, a carried optimization report with a broken link, X21 and owner-record checks weaker than their text, and playwright config risks.

findings.finding: On the package's own bootstrap, every .NET suite runner (including both corrected ones) exits 0 while running no test at all: the bootstrapped test projects use central package management, under which the F# SDK sets DisableImplicitFSharpCoreReference=true, and the locked test tooling (xunit 2.9.2, xunit.runner.visualstudio 2.8.2, Microsoft.NET.Test.Sdk 17.11.1) has no FSharp.Core. So FSharp.Core.dll is never deployed, and xunit skips every test assembly. The Causa.slnx-plus-filter form makes this quieter: each project reports 'No test matches the given testcase filter' and the run exits 0. Nothing in the package detects it. X21 is static, CI's bootstrap steps only build, and the suite-commands CI job and r9 suite-fixture use hand-written non-CPM projects with explicit package versions and implicit FSharp.Core, not the bootstrapped project files. This is inherited from v4.1.2 (its bootstrap differs from v4.1.4's only by playwright.config.ts), but it defeats what the amendment claims ('suite runners that execute', 'select exactly their tests'). Fixing it adds a package, and AGENT-RULES says 'No other package is added without an owner decision', so it needs an owner decision. The Rehearsal 009 run (7+7 tests) shows that application had FSharp.Core somehow. I could not tell from the repository how.
findings.evidence: v41 --package requirements-compiled/v4.1.4 --bootstrap <empty dir>, and again onto tools/requirements-compiler/tests/fixtures/conditor-0.10.18-scaffold. Added one [<Xunit.Fact>] in namespace Causa.Contract.Tests.Wire.Probe to tests/Causa.Contract.Tests/Wire/Producer.fs. Ran `dotnet test Causa.slnx --filter "FullyQualifiedName~Causa.Contract.Tests.|...App.Tests."`, which printed '[xUnit.net] Skipping: Causa.Contract.Tests (could not find dependent assembly 'FSharp.Core, Version=10.1.0')' for all six test projects, with exit 0. `dotnet msbuild tests/Causa.Contract.Tests/Causa.Contract.Tests.fsproj -getProperty:DisableImplicitFSharpCoreReference` gives true, ManagePackageVersionsCentrally gives true, and bin/ has no FSharp.Core.dll. Adding <PackageVersion Include="FSharp.Core" Version="10.1.402"/> and a PackageReference made the run report 'Passed: 1'. diff -r of the v4.1.2 and v4.1.4 bootstraps (bin/obj excluded) gives only 'Only in boot414: playwright.config.ts'. tools/r9/r9.fsx:741 writes fixture fsproj files with explicit Version= and no CPM.

findings.finding: The new checks are weaker than their text. (a) X21's 'names only projects it defines' is tautological: `defined` is planPlaywrightProjects, the projects the runners themselves name, and the config is generated from the same list, so the check can only fail when no configuration is declared. (b) X21 does not check that a corrected dotnet filter selects the same tests as the suite's matcher, or that the decision's `applies.suiteRunners` lists the suite. (c) The offline owner-record check (ScopeTests.ownerRecordProblems) checks that the approval records the decision id, not that it selected option A. I checked all three by hand, and they hold today.
findings.evidence: V41Package.fs runnerCheck: `let defined = if config = "" then [] else planPlaywrightProjects i`. ScopeTests.fs:333-347 reads only decision_id. My own simulation checked each of the 419 dotnet plan tests: under FullyQualifiedName-contains semantics plus project targeting, it is selected by exactly its suite's runner (0 mismatches). Each of the 373 playwright tests is selected by exactly one runner, by project and path (0 mismatches). ODR applies: -01 covers SU-OWN-DOTNET and SU-DOTNET-LIVE, -02 the four browser suites, which equals suiteRunners.

findings.finding: Risks in the bootstrapped playwright.config.ts. (a) It hard-codes a sandbox-specific executablePath, /opt/pw-browsers/chromium, into the competition repository. (b) One config, with a local python3 http.server webServer and baseURL http://127.0.0.1:4321, serves SU-BROWSER-LIVE too, whose fixture is 'the deployed candidate at the exact SHA'. The live suite will start and target a local static server unless integration changes the config or the tests override baseURL. (c) Conditor's chromium-only playwright.config.js, as AMENDMENT describes it, stays beside it. It has no owner in agent-file-ownership.json, and the recorded Conditor 0.10.18 fixture contains no playwright.config.js, so CI never tests the two configs together.
